audit_scope.description: Trust model for EIP-3044 (baseFee in RPC block response), EIP-747 (wallet_watchAsset), EIP-197 (bn128 pairing precompile), EIP-684 (contract address collision detection), and Prague fork structure. Covers RPC interface security, wallet token tracking, cryptographic precompile validation, code immutability enforcement, and fork activation.

in_scope: RPC block query with baseFee field (EIP-3044)
baseFee field validation against fork status
Prague fork activation and module initialization
Prague block processing and state roots

misclassified_entities.reason: EVM Contract Caller is an internal EVM component - smart contracts or EOAs calling precompiles via CALL opcode are part of the internal execution environment
Malicious Actor in EIP-684 security enforcement subgraph is a threat actor description used for attack modeling, not a legitimate external entity

trusted_external_entities.name: JSON-RPC Client
trusted_external_entities.rationale: External applications querying block information via JSON-RPC are untrusted. The node must correctly include or omit the baseFee field based on fork status. Pre-EIP-1559 blocks must not include baseFee; post-1559 blocks must include it.

trusted_external_entities.name: Web Application (dApp)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: dApps requesting token tracking may be malicious, attempting phishing via similar token names/symbols or SSRF via image URLs. Wallet must validate URI schemes (only https/ipfs/data), check for internal targets, perform token similarity detection, and return before user interaction to prevent fingerprinting.

trusted_external_entities.name: Contract Deployer
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: Contract creation via CREATE/CREATE2 or creation transaction
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Any entity can attempt contract deployment. EIP-684 collision detection must verify target address has nonce == 0 AND code.length == 0 before allowing deployment. Collision with existing contract triggers exception handling identical to invalid opcode.

trusted_external_entities.name: Consensus Layer
trusted_external_entities.rationale: The Consensus Layer communicates with the EL via the Engine API, authenticated with JWT. It provides fork activation signals for Prague fork transition. Semi-trusted because the channel is authenticated but CL bugs could send incorrect signals.

trusted_external_entities.name: Transaction Submitter
trusted_external_entities.rationale: External users submit transactions that must be parsed and validated according to Prague fork rules. Transaction validation includes field checks, signature verification, and gas requirements.

trusted_external_entities.name: Network Peer
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Network peers provide block data that must undergo full header validation, transaction processing, and state root verification. Peers can be malicious and attempt to propagate invalid blocks.

boundary_edges.security_assumption: RPC response must correctly determine fork status and include/exclude baseFee field accordingly. Post-1559 blocks missing baseFee in header indicate data corruption.

Wallet must validate URI schemes (reject file:// and http://), check for SSRF targeting internal services, detect token name/symbol similarity for phishing prevention, and return true immediately before user interaction to prevent fingerprinting.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: Contract creation pipeline with collision detection
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Before init code execution, the EVM must check target address for nonce > 0 OR code.length > 0. Collision triggers invalid opcode treatment: consume all gas, revert state changes, return zero address to caller.
Transactions must be parsed and validated according to Prague-specific rules. Invalid transactions are rejected before execution.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: Prague fork block processing and validation
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Block headers must pass validation. All transactions must be executed sequentially with correct state root computation. State root mismatch indicates invalid block.
Fork activation signals are authenticated via JWT. Prague fork modules must be properly initialized before processing begins. Executing Prague logic before activation would cause consensus failures.

coverage_gaps: EXT-EVM-CALLER for bn128 pairing precompile is misclassified - the actual external boundary is at the transaction submission level, which is covered by EXT-USER-PRAGUE and EXT-TX-SENDER from other batches
